theme: Cozy witch cottages with potion gardens

scout.suggestedAngle: Position the book as a "botanical spellcraft" coloring experience rather than a generic witch or cottage book: each page pairs a cozy cottage exterior/interior scene with a labeled potion-garden element (moonflower patches, mushroom rings, herb-drying racks, bubbling cauldrons fed by garden ingredients). Add small recurring details shoppers love in cottagecore niches — black cats, broomsticks, jars of ingredients, hand-lettered plant names — to create a distinct "cozy witch herbalist" sub-theme that differentiates from both plain Halloween witch books and plain cottage/fairy-house books, and supports upsell keywords around gardening, herbalism, and cottagecore fantasy.
scout.selectionRationale: This theme offers the best balance of the three key criteria. It rides the well-established, evergreen 'cozy/cottagecore witch' aesthetic that has consistent adult-colorist appeal and gets an added seasonal boost around Halloween/autumn without being purely seasonal (unlike a strictly holiday theme). The subject matter -- cottages, potion bottles, herb/potion gardens, familiars -- provides enough visual variety to fill a full-length book with intricate, non-repetitive designs, which is critical for adult coloring book quality and perceived value. While 'witch' and 'cottage' themes individually have competition on KDP, the specific combined angle of witch cottages PLUS potion gardens is a more differentiated, ownable niche than generic entries in either category, and it outperforms the alternatives: cactus gardens and rosemaling barns have narrower or already-saturated appeal, lighthouse keepers skews too niche/kid-oriented with uncertain keyword demand, and steampunk clockwork animals, while strong, has a smaller passionate-but-narrower fan base compared to the broad cozy-witch aesthetic's cross-over appeal with cottagecore, fantasy, and seasonal shoppers.
